basis: Catalogue reconciliation against the original 200-candidate register. This is not a fresh source audit of all 200, local validation or EA Selected approval. Original protection decisions remain unchanged.

Listening at public pub sessions, not a promise of joining musicians.
Municipal pool access with visitor etiquette, not a claim to local identity.

Named commercial bathhouse under its entry rules.
Advertised hosted lavash introduction, not access to any Armenian household.

Public craft introduction, not mastery or unrestricted artisan access.

Specific advertised agricultural encounter, not any boat trip or unsupervised farm work.
Public palenque visit, without guaranteed production steps or field work.
One-hour public Arte Añil workshop using the studio's provided scarf or T-shirt. No personal garments, mastery claim or wider authority over Salvadoran indigo traditions is implied.
Publicly advertised introduction, not permission to enter every local bomba occasion.

Publicly offered Indigenous-guided programme only. Original protected-candidate status remains. No broader cultural access or local EA validation is inferred.
An Edinburgh public event is not the original village-hall setting. The original candidate remains unresolved.
Named visitor introduction, not access to other towers or unsupervised bell handling.

Public dining at the named Heuriger, not vineyard or cellar entry.
Public coffee and hospitality introduction, not entry to a private majlis.

Independent public meal, not following a stall behind the counter.
Named public processing tour, not guaranteed cacao harvesting.
Public peña hospitality, subject to the venue's programme and booking terms.
Public museum exhibition and observation through a glass hive. Bee handling, apiary access and a hands-on workshop are not promised.
The public museum, outdoor tree exhibit and processing story make mastiha legible but do not fulfil the original promise of joining a working harvest.
A confirmed visit to one named farm from the current official guide. The exact activity varies by host, and parade participation or unrestricted family and farm access are not promised.

A public visitor gallery, production exhibition, cellar view and tasting at the Appenzeller demonstration dairy. It does not fulfil the original pasture visit or provide ordinary hands-on cheese making.

Observation from clearly public or visitor-permitted areas at Ajman Creek. Yard entry, builder interaction, tool handling, a managed tour and active construction at a particular time are not promised.

A prearranged public trek with a farmer acting as local guide on the route offered by Jatiluwih tourism village. It does not open every field, irrigation structure, temple, ritual or community decision to visitors.

An advance reservation at one named Pinglin farm for the seasonal picking and production steps confirmed by the host. A complete processing cycle, every tea variety and a fixed take-home result are not promised.

A route booked with an operator currently listed by Navajo Nation Parks and Recreation. Original protected-candidate status remains. No access beyond the guide-led route and no right to record or repeat every place, name or story is inferred.

Careful observation from a clearly public approach along Bulukumba's officially listed working boatbuilding coast. Entry to a yard, worker interaction, active construction, a managed tour and access to close technique or ritual knowledge are not promised.
MATA's two-day beginner Silver Weekend when a group and teacher are available. The exact artisan, studio, design and advanced technique remain outside the promise until confirmed for the session.

A named public Cantonese Mahjong basics class at PMQ, not entry to a neighbourhood association, family table, commercial mahjong school or gambling setting. Rules and scoring apply to the taught format.

An announced paid public rose-picking ritual within the official Kazanlak Rose Festival programme. It is not entry to an ordinary commercial harvest, permission to use another field or evidence that a brief visitor activity constitutes agricultural work.

Public seated spectatorship at a named Siem Reap hospitality venue that currently advertises Sbek Thom. The original maker meeting, a ceremonial performance, backstage access, puppet handling and a guaranteed timetable are not promised.

Ordinary access to Museu do Cante followed by a separately announced public performance when available. Spontaneous tavern singing, a private rehearsal and a guaranteed live chorus on an ordinary museum visit are outside the promise.

A current public Red Dao herbal-bath service at Dao's Care in Hanoi. This is not a Tả Phìn village or household visit, herb foraging, access to a family recipe, or evidence of community-led delivery in the original location.

A public visit to the named Antemoro paper workshop in Ambalavao to observe the process and finished work. Hands-on paper making, flower placement and a take-home sheet are not promised unless the workshop confirms them for that visit.

A current ninety-minute visit and tasting at Cloçon Téla's urban chocolate factory in São Tomé. This is not a roça stay, pod harvest, access to every production step or a complete account of the islands' cacao and forced-labour history.

A self-guided evening walk on ordinary public routes documented by Tirana Municipality. This is not a staged ceremony, resident-led tour, guaranteed crowd or permission to photograph people using their own city.

A current visit to the public documentation centre, followed by respectful spectatorship only if a future Whit Tuesday date and visitor arrangements are officially announced. Open tourist participation in the procession is not promised.

A paid public Cultural Village programme in Apia with hosted umu preparation and lunch. This is not preparation inside a private village or household, a Sunday invitation, guaranteed hands-on cooking or access beyond the published programme.
A named public beginner va'a paddling introduction on Moorea. This is not the original traditional-navigation lesson, a racing session, open-ocean travel or proof of mastery.

A public excursion to observe the manual paper process at the Meros mill in Konigil. This is not the original hands-on papermaking promise, proof of an unchanged medieval process or guaranteed access to every working area.

A visitor-centre-arranged weaving tour in Bonwire with a published introductory try at selected spinning, warping and weaving stages. This is not mastery, unrestricted workshop access or permission to copy a named pattern without context.

newSourceReviews.finding: Uzbekistan Travel currently publishes factory excursions at the Meros paper mill that show manual production from natural materials. A government directorate's 2025 gallery independently states that the operating process remains manual and visible to visitors, but neither source promises hands-on papermaking.
newSourceReviews.nextAction: Keep the guide observation-led. Recheck hours, price, language, visitor route and whether any hands-on format is directly published by 14 December 2026.

newSourceReviews.finding: Visit Ghana currently publishes a Bonwire visitor-centre route, daily hours, contact number, community workshop visit and introductory try at thread spinning, warping and weaving. Museum evidence supports the narrow-strip construction and cultural context of Asante kente.
newSourceReviews.nextAction: Require visitors to arrange the tour through the centre and confirm the current fee, group size and practical task. Recheck the offer by 14 December 2026 and keep private workspaces outside the promise.

newSourceReviews.finding: Samoa Tourism currently publishes a paid Tuesday to Friday Cultural Village programme in Apia that includes umu preparation. Its food and Apia guides separately state that the programme serves an umu-cooked lunch.
newSourceReviews.nextAction: Keep the public Cultural Village distinct from a private Sunday meal. Recheck hours, price, meal inclusion and dietary arrangements by 14 December 2026. Do not promise hands-on preparation.

newSourceReviews.finding: Tahiti Tourisme currently lists We Do Va'a in Haapiti as a small family operator offering a beginner va'a introduction with experienced rowers. The listing supports paddling but not the original traditional-navigation lesson and contains conflicting opening-day information.
newSourceReviews.nextAction: Require the visitor to confirm day, price, route, equipment and conditions directly. Keep traditional navigation, racing and open-ocean travel outside the promise. Recheck by 14 December 2026.

newSourceReviews.finding: AAT Aorn and Norfolk Island Tourism currently publish a one-hour Norf'k language class on Wednesday and Thursday at Governors Lodge with a direct booking route. The reviewed gallery contains attractive but generic island and heritage photographs rather than the language, classroom or a defensible learning context.
newSourceReviews.nextAction: Keep the access evidence and candidate priority. Do not publish until an exact, high-quality and responsibly creditable photograph shows the language or learning context without exposing schoolchildren or implying a private lesson.

newSourceReviews.finding: Tirana Municipality's sustainable mobility guide explicitly documents pedestrian Embassy Row becoming an evening xhiro promenade. Current national tourism and locally reported sources support the wider public-space context, but no fixed route, start time or crowd is guaranteed.
newSourceReviews.nextAction: Keep this self-guided and non-performative. Recheck the municipal route, lighting and public access by 13 December 2026, and do not present residents as subjects supplied for visitor photography.

newSourceReviews.finding: Mullerthal currently publishes ordinary access, exhibits, contact details and changing hours for the Hopping Procession Documentation Centre. Its live-event page confirms the annual Whit Tuesday pattern and public spectatorship but marks the next date as coming soon.
newSourceReviews.nextAction: Keep the documentation centre as the current route. Do not promote a live visit until the official date, route and spectator guidance are published, and never infer open tourist participation.

newSourceReviews.finding: Visit Barbados provides strong current context, suggests places where road tennis may be seen and encourages visitors to learn. The reviewed sources do not identify a current public beginner session, named road-tennis coach, reliable timetable or direct booking route.
newSourceReviews.nextAction: Keep the candidate off the catalogue until a named public road-tennis lesson or announced tournament with dependable access is published. Do not substitute lawn-tennis coaching or arrive at a community court expecting players to host visitors.

newSourceReviews.finding: Several resellers still advertise Ibo dhow safaris, but the current regional listing for Ibo Island Lodge states that the lodge is closed and its reopening date is unknown. Older itineraries therefore do not prove dependable present access.
newSourceReviews.nextAction: Keep the candidate off the catalogue. Require a current operating provider, direct booking route, vessel and weather-safety information and a clear crew-benefit boundary before reconsideration.

newSourceReviews.finding: The original loko iʻa proposal depends on each Native Hawaiian organisation choosing whether it wants visitor visibility and has capacity for a workday. A public volunteer page alone does not grant EA authority to scale or editorially package that invitation.
newSourceReviews.nextAction: Do not publish or contact organisations in the current no-consent work phase. Reconsider only within a future holder-led process that confirms capacity, visibility, safety, data and photography boundaries.

newSourceReviews.finding: Dao's Care currently publishes Red Dao herbal baths at its Hanoi social-enterprise treatment centre. Vietnam's national tourism site explains the broader Tả Phìn bath tradition, but the previously named lodge route is closed and current public evidence does not establish the original village household encounter.
newSourceReviews.nextAction: Keep Hanoi and Tả Phìn visibly distinct. Recheck the treatment menu, reservation route, current location and social-enterprise claims by 13 December 2026. Do not imply access to a family recipe or village life.

newSourceReviews.finding: The named Ambalavao workshop currently publishes visitor hours, a location and direct contact for observing Antemoro paper production. The available public page does not clearly promise that ordinary visitors can make a sheet themselves.
newSourceReviews.nextAction: Publish observation only. Recheck opening hours and contact route by 13 December 2026, and require direct confirmation before describing any hands-on step or take-home result.

newSourceReviews.finding: Cloçon Téla currently publishes a ninety-minute São Tomé factory visit with chocolate tasting, appointment request and a listed price of 125 STN. The public route supports an urban bean-to-bar introduction, not the original broader farm and harvest premise.
newSourceReviews.nextAction: Keep the urban-factory, appointment and historical-context boundaries explicit. Recheck price, duration and booking availability by 13 December 2026 before presenting live access.

newSourceReviews.finding: Kazanlak Municipality's completed 2026 festival programme listed paid public rose-picking rituals near Yasenovo and Kazanlak plus separate distilling demonstrations. This proves a recurring visitor-facing format but not the next edition, access to an ordinary commercial harvest or a future crop condition.
newSourceReviews.nextAction: Keep the guide date-explicit and unavailable for booking until the next official programme is published. Recheck the village, meeting point, ticket route, transport and programme-change notice before promoting a live date.

newSourceReviews.finding: Sompoli Dthan currently states that its Siem Reap cultural restaurant offers Khmer Sbek Thom and small shadow-puppet performance with the Reamker story. The website provides a public contact but no detailed timetable, duration, price or maker encounter.
newSourceReviews.nextAction: Retain public spectatorship only. Recheck the current performance night, format, price, language support and reservation route by 13 December 2026. Do not reinstate the original maker meeting without explicit public evidence.

newSourceReviews.finding: Portugal's national tourism site directs visitors to Museu do Cante in Serpa and recommends checking local tourist offices for planned performances while describing informal singing as spontaneous. This supports a museum-first route and separately announced public listening, not a guaranteed live encounter.
newSourceReviews.nextAction: Keep spontaneous singing outside the visitor promise. Recheck museum hours and a named public performance before suggesting a live date, and preserve the distinction between interpretation, formal performance and informal social singing.

newSourceReviews.finding: Bulukumba's tourism department currently lists the working boatbuilding coast across four Bonto Bahari villages as a visitor site where ships can be observed under construction. The page publishes no booking method, managed package or reliable staffed hours, so the original yard premise is narrowed to safe public observation.
newSourceReviews.nextAction: Keep the public-edge and active-workplace boundaries prominent. Recheck the local visitor listing, safe approach and separate 2026 festival page by 13 December 2026.

newSourceReviews.finding: MATA currently lists Silver Weekend as a beginner filigree workshop over two days at four hours per day for four to six participants, with materials included and a small project. Timing, teacher and venue depend on the formed group.
newSourceReviews.nextAction: Keep the need for written confirmation of date, teacher, venue, language, price and inclusions explicit. Recheck the workshop listing by 13 December 2026.

newSourceReviews.finding: Glocal Mahjong currently publishes a two-hour Cantonese Mahjong basics class for two to four participants at PMQ in Central, with daily advance-booking windows, three delivery languages and a route for solo visitors to join scheduled classes.
newSourceReviews.nextAction: Keep the named beginner class distinct from private, neighbourhood and gambling settings. Recheck schedule, venue, price and public booking route by 13 December 2026.

newSourceReviews.finding: Indonesia's Ministry of Tourism village platform currently lists a public Jatiluwih trek with a farmer acting as local guide and a direct village contact route. UNESCO establishes the living subak context and its tourism pressures. This supports a bounded guided trail, not unrestricted field, irrigation, temple or ritual access.
newSourceReviews.nextAction: Keep the farmer-led public route and living-landscape limits explicit. Recheck the listing, guide arrangement and current visitor conditions by 13 December 2026.

newSourceReviews.finding: New Taipei City Travel currently identifies Green Light Tea Plantation and its owner, marks the farm open by appointment and advertises tea picking and tea production by advance reservation. This supports one named farm route, subject to seasonal steps and direct confirmation.
newSourceReviews.nextAction: Keep the named-farm, advance-reservation and seasonal-processing boundaries explicit. Recheck public access and the listing's differing telephone fields by 13 December 2026.

newSourceReviews.finding: Navajo Nation Parks and Recreation currently publishes an authorised Monument Valley operator list, seasonal hours, 2026 fees and independent-drive restrictions. One listed operator publicly offers a guided backcountry route. This supports only the selected guide-led programme and does not relax the original protection review.
newSourceReviews.nextAction: Preserve the operator-list, guide authority, route and recording boundaries at every surface. Recheck the current list, fees and park conditions by 13 December 2026.

newSourceReviews.finding: The Appenzeller demonstration dairy currently publishes ordinary admission to a self-guided exhibition overlooking daily cheese production, with a cellar view, tasting and written smartphone translations. This is strong public access to production, but it does not include the original pasture component or ordinary hands-on cheese making.
newSourceReviews.nextAction: Keep the visitor-gallery, group-workshop and pasture distinctions explicit. Recheck hours, production timing and exhibition access by 13 December 2026.

newSourceReviews.finding: Ajman Tourism currently identifies the creekside Dhow Yard as a place where visitors can watch craftsmen at work. It publishes a location but no hours, formal tour or permission to enter work zones, so the original premise is narrowed to careful public observation.
newSourceReviews.nextAction: Keep current-access confirmation and the public-edge boundary prominent. Recheck the official visitor page and exact approach by 13 December 2026.

newSourceReviews.finding: The Vama Egg Museum publishes a visitor workshop with Letitia Orsivschi and multilingual interpretation, but the reviewed exact official photographs do not meet EA's current high-end visual threshold at guide and card scale.
newSourceReviews.nextAction: Retain the public-workshop evidence and keep the candidate off the catalogue until a current, exact and responsibly creditable photograph meets the publication standard.

newSourceReviews.finding: The official 2026 Sinjska Alka programme confirms that this year's public event took place from 7 to 9 August. The year-round museum is a possible related alternative, but it does not resolve the original live-event candidate.
newSourceReviews.nextAction: Wait for the next confirmed public event calendar, or separately evaluate the museum only if its access and exact photography justify a related-alternative guide.

newSourceReviews.finding: The current Rio visitor page found in this review documents the completed 2026 samba-school rehearsal season. It does not yet establish a future public rehearsal that an ordinary visitor can plan around.
newSourceReviews.nextAction: Recheck when the next official public rehearsal calendar is released. Do not present a past schedule as current access.

newSourceReviews.finding: The House of the Carniolan Bee currently publishes an ordinary visitor route to an exhibition with virtual interpretation and real glass hives containing living bees. This supports a museum encounter in Višnja Gora, not bee handling, an apiary visit or the original broader hands-on premise.
newSourceReviews.nextAction: Keep the glass-hive and ordinary-admission boundary explicit. Recheck the exhibition, live-hive status and visitor access by 13 December 2026.

newSourceReviews.finding: Chios Mastic Museum currently offers a public exhibition, outdoor mastic-tree habitat and processing interpretation. This provides strong public access to the material and its system, but it does not establish visitor participation in a working mastiha harvest.
newSourceReviews.nextAction: Publish only as a museum alternative. Continue looking for a clearly public, current harvest programme before narrowing the original hands-on candidate.

newSourceReviews.finding: Medellín's official 2026 visitor material lists nearly seventeen Santa Elena farms and describes year-round garden visits, family interpretation and silleta making context. Some, but not all, farms advertise small hands-on or food additions, so the visitor must confirm one specific host and format.
newSourceReviews.nextAction: Keep the farm-by-farm variation visible and recheck the official directory and direct access route by 13 December 2026.

newSourceReviews.finding: Current public sources support a Konigil paper-making visitor route near Samarkand, but the reviewed exact-source photographs did not meet EA's current publication standard at guide and card scale.
newSourceReviews.nextAction: Keep the candidate off the public catalogue until an exact, high-quality and responsibly creditable photograph and a current direct access route can be verified together.

newSourceReviews.finding: The Bayou Vermilion District currently publishes a recurring Sunday Cajun or zydeco dance route in Lafayette. Reviewed official and licensed photographs did not yet meet EA's high-end visual threshold without becoming generic or dated.
newSourceReviews.nextAction: Keep the candidate off the public catalogue while retaining the current programme evidence. Recheck for a stronger exact photograph and live schedule before publication.

newSourceReviews.finding: Mooska and Visit Estonia currently describe a prebooked farm walk of about one and a half hours through three smoke saunas, with interpretation of construction, heating, family traditions and meat smoking followed by a tasting. This supports a public learning visit, not the original implication of bathing or private ritual participation.
newSourceReviews.nextAction: Maintain the walk and bathing-session distinction at every surface. Recheck access, dietary details and the public route by 12 December 2026.

newSourceReviews.finding: Cyprus Taste Tours currently publishes a seven-to-eight-hour Halloumi Heaven route with listed coastal pickup areas, hands-on halloumi and anari making, brunch and three route-dependent food stops. This supports a full-day public tour, not an independently bookable cheese workshop at a fixed village.
newSourceReviews.nextAction: Keep the variable route and dietary caveats visible. Recheck the current itinerary and public booking route by 12 December 2026.

newSourceReviews.finding: Arte Añil currently publishes a one-hour English or Spanish indigo workshop with advance reservation, materials and protective items included, and a choice of the studio's scarf or T-shirt. The provider explicitly says not to bring a personal item for dyeing.
newSourceReviews.nextAction: Keep the provided-item boundary explicit and recheck session times, public booking and accessibility by 12 December 2026.

newSourceReviews.finding: The Museum of Kraków announces a public 2026 competition arrival, procession and exhibition. Its current adult beginner series has only nine places, is marked full and is designed for people who have entered or intend to enter the competition. Family sessions require a multi-date commitment and children. Neither establishes the original casual visitor workshop with a local craftsperson.
newSourceReviews.nextAction: Keep the public arrival as a related alternative. Recheck for a future openly bookable beginner workshop that suits an ordinary visitor before narrowing the original candidate.

newSourceReviews.finding: The official June 2026 four-page brochure and current tourism and shellfish-committee pages establish a publicly offered oyster outing, authorised professional roster, central reservation route, three-to-six-hour duration and cancellation terms. The original work-the-beds premise is narrowed to observation and host-controlled participation, with no independent activity at the beds.
newSourceReviews.nextAction: Maintain the dated public-guide review and media record. This does not grant local validation or EA Selected status.

newSourceReviews.finding: The Museum of Sarajevo's official 26 August 2026 notice closes Damir Imamovic's eighteen-Wednesday season. It supports the past programme, not an upcoming bookable sevdalinka performance. The Sarajevo coffee guide is not a substitute for this music candidate.
newSourceReviews.nextAction: Find a current, publicly announced sevdalinka performance and verify date, venue, visitor access and a suitable photograph. Do not publish the ended weekly season as current.
